note:
Second concrete instance — the blind spot is broader than the filed body states: TWO distinct out-root subpaths, on two different pods, in the same run

The filed body cites arm 3's capture layout `<out_root>/logs/capture-*.slotN.log`. Arm 1's fits
phase, same issue and same session, uses a DIFFERENT out-root subpath:

    /workspace/issue2546/work/fits_a1/slot{0,1,2,3}.log

So the gap is not "one dispatcher chose an unusual logs/ dir" — two phases of one experiment
independently put worker logs under the out-root at two different depths, and neither matches
any of the poller's three globs. Any fix keyed narrowly on `<out_root>/logs/` would close the
arm-3 instance and leave the arm-1 instance open.

Measured impact on arm 1 (`pod-2546-arm1c`, phase `p5_fits`, 71 registry jobs over 4 workers):

- the parent dispatcher log legitimately freezes at its fan-out line for the whole phase —
  correct behavior for a fan-out parent, since per-unit progress belongs to the workers
- consequence: `last_log_mtime_sec_ago` reached 2971 s (~50 min) while
  `phase_log_mtime_sec_ago` and `shard_log_mtime_sec_ago` both sat at the 1e9 not-found
  sentinel
- meanwhile the run was demonstrably healthy: 29/71 units complete, 33 claimed, 4 workers live,
  all four slot logs written within the last ~15 s, `session_cpu_secs` 57,252 -> 142,910 across
  31 min of wall
- the per-unit progress lines the convention requires DO exist and are correctly shaped
  (`[p5] unit k/N`, 6/8/8/7 across the four slots) — they are simply in files the poller cannot
  see

Worth noting for whoever implements this: the visible-progress signal and the invisible-log
problem are independent. The driver is compliant with the per-unit progress-line convention
(`.claude/rules/code-style.md`, T2 trigger at >~50 units); the defect is purely that the poller's
glob set cannot reach worker logs placed under an arbitrary out-root. A reviewer diagnosing this
from the parent log alone would wrongly conclude the driver omits progress lines — I made exactly
that error before probing the pod, which is some evidence the blind spot costs diagnostic time
beyond the false `stalled` verdict itself.

Also relevant to option (3) in the filed body (a bounded search under common pod roots): on arm 1
the layout is two directory levels below the out-root with an arm-suffixed parent name
(`work/fits_a1/`), so a shallow or fixed-depth probe would miss it.
